author: althoufx
text:
Thank you MM first for the prompt reply, as it happens in RTM more rarely from a while !

Yes i know those pics, they practically show to where (and why..)the price moves, and i set my entries according with them at 100%. Let's say they work perfectly, so no matter in catching moves and directions. But entries in RT are nice since the points are close to the extremities...otherwise price moves furher against after the entry (it happens always to me) and the pain begins...will it reverse?...yes, for sure, but where? For example: entering in a good trend in the middle, it results always in immediate strong reaction against, by price. It looks like the market was more interested in my failure then in its original path.

Also PAZ is a powerful concept, i think, but it has to be used very carefully because it's true that a hit into a PAZ makes the price going sure all through long, but not directly...

not straight...many things can happen from the hit to the completion... All the best MM!!

I was reading over the flag limits thread and noted 2 posts (one from Harry and one from Pedini). Can someone clear something up as I am a bit confused, which is more important? An engulf of a flag or FTB from flag?

I feel that the two posts are expressing different things, maybe it is down to preference or maybe I'm wrong.

Harry wrote: rcmacf wrote: Harry, I love the BBQ trade. I had a happy "In the Shower" trade this morning on Cable.

Here's some other stuff on there. Is there some way I could have stayed out of my lower, earlier short. I wasn't in this trade at all, but would have been.

Thanks.

1. after engulf of FL yes, sign we could be going lower. but i took a TT so i couldnt know it would engulf at the time.

2. remember that the FTB to FL is a higher probability trade than the trade you suggest (after engulf of FL to wait for return for a cap to take a short).

Pedini wrote: Hey DT - When doing your studies on the FL remember this: One of the most important parts of a FL is when it is engulfed.
